how_it_wins:
Land a commander, grow it off card flow, protect it, and hit one seat for 21 commander damage. Shabraz takes a +1/+1 counter and 1 life for every card you draw. Brallin takes a +1/+1 counter for every card you discard and pings each opponent for 1. A loot pays both commanders once. A seven-card wheel pays both seven times.

The board picks the commander. Shabraz is the default: he flies, and Teferi's Ageless Insight, Bard, King of Dale, Alhammarret's Archive, Lae'zel and Knowledge Is Power all scale him. Brallin is the pick when Torbran, Gratuitous Violence or Fiery Emancipation is out. Torbran adds only to red sources and Shabraz is white-blue, so Torbran never helps him.

On the turn you swing, three things have to be true. A commander has survived a turn cycle. A double-strike or evasion piece is reachable: Blade Historian, Embercleave, Fireshrieker, Genji Glove, Lizard Blades, Akroma's Will, Boros Charm; Brotherhood Regalia, Key to the City, Zephyr Boots. A shield is held, and Flawless Maneuver is free with a commander out.

The wheels are finishers. Cast one with a commander already on the battlefield, never as early tempo. Stack 001 is why: Windfall for seven with both commanders out is 7 to each opponent, 7 life, and two 10/10s. Double strike on a 10/10 is 20, one short, so the kill turn needs one more counter or pump: Lae'zel, Knowledge Is Power, or Embercleave's +1/+1. That is arithmetic, not a stack. No passing stack resolves combat in this deck, so the stated win needs a stack scenario.

Brallin's pings are not commander damage; only combat damage counts toward 21. They are still a clock on every seat at once: stacks 004 and 005 put 21 on each opponent from seven discards, with Artist's Talent at level 3 or with Torbran.

What the table misreads: a loot deck and two 3/3s. One wheel later it is a 10/10 flyer, and every 21 removes a seat.
mulligan:
Keep a hand that can put a commander on the table and do something while it waits. Your rule from game 002: at most one wheel, and at least one body or one ramp piece. A hand of lands and wheels does nothing until a commander lands, and then it has nothing left to cast.

Lands: keep two to four. The deck runs 36. Across 10,000 seeded first sevens, 1,914 had one land or none, 3,017 had two, 2,903 three, 1,573 four, and 593 five or more. Keep two lands only with a rock: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Azorius or Izzet Signet, either Talisman. With Smothering Tithe that group of seven is in 41.2% of opening sevens. Sol Ring is what made game 001 fast.

Check white. Shabraz costs {3}{W}{U}, and white is the thin colour: 19 land sources against a target of 22, on curve 0.866 from lands alone and 0.907 with rocks. Brallin needs one {R}, and red has 34 land sources. A hand with no white source is a Brallin-first hand; keep it only if it casts Brallin on turn four.

Cards that make a keep: Stoneforge Mystic (finds Lightning Greaves or Embercleave), Faithless Looting, Sorcerer Class, Kitsa, Collector's Vault. Cheap card flow now pays both commanders later. Gemstone Caverns, when you are not the starting player, can begin on the battlefield making any colour; it costs one card from hand.

Ship a hand that passes the land count and fails the body-or-ramp rule. The goldfish mulligans by lands alone and keeps its first seven in 0.799 of games; of the hands it kept, 0.76 also pass your rule. About one kept hand in four needs your judgment, not the land count.

Do not keep for the kill pieces. Blade Historian, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation do nothing until a commander is out.

combo_lines.001:
Proven on an older list. Library of Leng, Sticky Fingers and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove sat in the discarded hand and Hallowed Fountain was a land; all four have left the 99. None of them did anything in this line. Windfall, Brallin and Shabraz are all in v2.0.0, and the line stands.

It turns on when the fourteen triggers go on the stack. Windfall's discard and draw are one resolution, and no player gets priority inside it. Brallin is a 3/3 with no counters through the discard and through all seven draws. Only after Windfall finishes do the seven Brallin triggers and seven Shabraz triggers go on the stack, in the order you choose.

What it proves: one Brallin trigger per card you discard, so 7 to each opponent, 40 to 33. The opponents' discards pay him nothing. Seven counters on each commander, two 10/10s, and 7 life.

What it does not prove: anything about combat. Double strike on a 10/10 Shabraz is 20, one short of 21; which extra card closes the gap needs a stack scenario. It does show why the commander comes first: a wheel with no commander out is card flow and nothing else.
combo_lines.002:
Proven on an older list, and the line cannot be played on v2.0.0: Library of Leng has left the deck, as have Sticky Fingers, Treasure Map // Treasure Cove and Hallowed Fountain from the scenario. Read it for the two rules it settles, not as a play.

First: a replacement effect that moves a discarded card somewhere other than the graveyard does not stop it being a discard. Brallin triggered four times, 4 to each opponent. No card in v2.0.0 moves a discarded card that way, so this rule waits for a card that uses it.

Second, and this one is live: Windfall draws every player cards equal to the greatest number any one player discarded. Here one opponent discarded five, so everyone drew five, you included with four discarded. If you hold the biggest hand, you set the draw for the whole table; if an opponent does, they set yours. Jace's Archivist reads the same way. Reforge the Soul draws everyone seven whatever was discarded.

What it does not prove: Shabraz was not on the battlefield, so the draw half is unpriced here.
combo_lines.003:
Proven on an older list. Library of Leng has left the deck, as have Sticky Fingers and Hallowed Fountain from the scenario. Raugrin Triome and Brallin are both in v2.0.0, and the Brallin half of the line stands. The Leng half, that Leng cannot catch a discard paid as a cost, no longer applies to anything you play.

It turns on cost against effect. Discarding Raugrin Triome to pay its cycling cost is still a discard, so Brallin triggers. His trigger goes on the stack above the cycling ability and resolves first: one counter, 1 damage to each opponent, then you draw.

That gives you a ping at instant speed without a wheel. Three cards in v2.0.0 cycle: Raugrin Triome ({3}), Glittering Massif ({2}) and Marauding Mako ({2}). If a seat is at 1, cycle in response and the ping lands before the draw. Key to the City's discard is also a cost by its oracle text, but this stack did not resolve it; treat it as the same shape, unproven.

What it does not prove: Shabraz was off the board, so whether the cycle's draw also pays him is not tested here.
combo_lines.004:
Proven on an older list. Magmakin Artillerist was the second damage source in this scenario and has left the deck; so have Sticky Fingers, Treasure Map // Treasure Cove, Swiftfoot Boots and Hallowed Fountain from the hand and board. The Brallin half stands, and it is the half you can play.

It turns on per-event replacement. Artist's Talent at level 3 adds 2 to each noncombat damage event from a source you control. Brallin's seven triggers are seven events, so each ping is 1 + 2 = 3 and seven discards are 21 to each opponent. The extra 2 is dealt by Brallin, not by the Talent. His counters are unchanged: seven, a 10/10.

What it does not prove: getting there. Level 3 is stipulated. Casting the Talent and buying both levels is {1}{R}, {2}{R}, {2}{R}, eight mana in all. Level 3 reads noncombat only, so it adds nothing to a commander's swing, and pings never count toward 21. With Torbran also out, each ping would take both additions; that combination needs a stack scenario.
combo_lines.005:
Proven on an older list. Spider-Man, New Champion was the second damage source and has left the deck, as has Swiftfoot Boots from the hand. The Brallin and Torbran half stands.

It turns on the same per-event rule as stack 004, from a different card. Torbran adds 2 to each damage event a red source you control deals to an opponent. Brallin is red, so each of his seven pings is 3: 21 to each opponent. From 40 that is not a kill. It takes every seat to 19 and leaves the swing to finish one.

The stack stipulates Windfall's seven discards and does not resolve Windfall; that leg is stack 001.

What it does not prove: Torbran on combat damage. By oracle text he adds 2 to each of Brallin's combat-damage events too, so twice under double strike. Whether that extra counts toward 21 has no passing stack, and neither does Torbran with Gratuitous Violence, where the damaged player orders the two. Both need a stack scenario. Shabraz is white-blue, so Torbran never adds to him.

threat_assessment:
No game has been played on v2.0.0. The evidence is two games on older lists and five stacks; the table reads are assumptions.

WHEN YOU STOP BEING IGNORED. Turns one to four, the table sees a loot deck and two 3/3s. That read ends at any of four signals.
- Counters on a commander. The goldfish reads mean commander counters of 8.8 by turn six and 20.806 by turn eight; it has no removal, so that is a ceiling.
- A wheel resolving with a commander out. Stack 001: 7 to each seat and two 10/10s off one Windfall.
- Torbran or a level-3 Artist's Talent beside Brallin. Stacks 005 and 004: 21 to every seat off seven discards. A table that has seen it removes Brallin on sight.
- Smothering Tithe or Rhystic Study resolving. Both tax the whole table and both are Game Changers.

WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT. Put the loudest piece down last. Land a commander on a quiet turn behind Lightning Greaves or Champion's Helm. Hold the wheel, and fire it on the turn a double-strike piece and a shield are also in reach.

COUNT THEIR MANA BEFORE YOU COMMIT. Assumption: a blue seat with two open holds a counter; a seat with four open holds removal or a sweeper. Match the shield to the threat.
- Flawless Maneuver: free with a commander out; indestructible only. Exile, bounce and -X/-X go through.
- Akroma's Will: with a commander out, both modes, including protection from each colour and indestructible. Colourless removal goes through.
- Loran's Escape: hexproof and indestructible on one creature for {W}.
- Silence: no opponent casts a spell this turn; abilities still work. Cast it before the wheel.
- Negate: noncreature spells only.

THE GREAVES TRAP. Shroud stops your own targeting too. On a commander wearing Lightning Greaves you cannot equip anything else, attach Embercleave, cast Boros Charm's double strike, put Inti's counter on it, or use the commanders' cross-grants. Move Greaves first (equip {0}), or win with untargeted pieces: Blade Historian, Akroma's Will, Knowledge Is Power, Gratuitous Violence. Champion's Helm's hexproof stops opponents only.

TWO TAXES. Each recast from the command zone costs {2} more per earlier cast. Brallin was removed twice in game 001. Command Beacon (your commander) and Campfire (every commander you own) put a commander in hand; that cast skips the tax, it does not reset it.

WHAT YOU CANNOT ANSWER. No card in the 99 removes an enchantment or touches a graveyard, and Prismari Command is the one artifact answer. Against a resolved lock piece, win first.
matchups:
Named by shape and anchored to cards and the two logged games. Read the seat, not the commander.

SWEEPER CONTROL. You are the beatdown: the long game is theirs, and a symmetrical wheel refills them too. Assume the wrath. Commit one commander and keep the other in the command zone as the rebuild. Against a wrath, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm's indestructible mode, Akroma's Will and March of Swirling Mist save the board; Lightning Greaves and Champion's Helm do not. Use the one-sided refills: Tolarian Winds and Fateful Showdown discard and redraw your hand only, and Khorvath's Fury lets you name each opponent a foe, so they take damage instead of cards.

COUNTERSPELLS AND DRAW-GO (Steven, game 001). Resolve the commander when the blue seat is tapped. Win through what does not need to resolve on the kill turn: the commanders' triggers, Equipment already attached, Flawless Maneuver cast free. Silence before the wheel stops every response that is a spell. Do not wheel a blue seat into a fresh seven unless the wheel itself is lethal.

GO-WIDE TOKENS (Stuart's zombies, game 001). Brallin's pings hit players, not creatures. Your sweeps: Iroh's Demonstration (1 to each creature an opponent controls) and Incendiary Command (2 to each creature, yours included). Go over the board: Shabraz flies, Zephyr Boots flies Brallin, Brotherhood Regalia and Key to the City make a commander unblockable. Hit the token seat first. Shabraz gains 1 life per draw, doubled under Alhammarret's Archive.

COMBO. You are the beatdown, and your stack interaction is Negate and Silence. Spend Negate on the combo piece, not on protecting your own swing. Swords to Plowshares is the one removal spell that exiles, and Teferi, Master of Time's -3 phases a creature out until its controller's next turn.

STAX AND ENCHANTMENT LOCKS. No card in the 99 removes an enchantment; Negate on the way in is the answer. The engine is two creature triggers, so a spell tax costs you less than an equip tax. Race it.

GRAVEYARD DECKS. Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Jace's Archivist and Incendiary Command's wheel mode fill every graveyard. Loot instead: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Kitsa and Teferi, Master of Time put only your cards there.

TWO SEATS IN ONE TURN. Each 21 removes one opponent and leaves two with free shots at you. Genji Glove and Karlach each add a combat phase, so a grown commander could hit a second seat. That needs a stack scenario.
